newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria places $50 mln T-notes in bank bailout.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria places $50 mln T-notes in bank bailout.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry placed $50 million of 18-month, floater coupon T-notes with the country's biggest state-owned Bulbank under a stabilisation plan for the ailing state Biochimbank, the central bank said.

The paper bears a semi-annual coupon equal to the six-month LIBOR for the two working days prior to the six-month interest payment period plus three percentage points, the central bank said in a statement.
The issue was dated April 8 and was numbered BG 2030097112. The principal is redeemable at maturity.
Under a government decree the Finance ministry placed the issue with Bulbank to fund the buy-back of $50 million of dollar-denominated bad debt (ZUNK) bonds at par value from Biochimbank's portfolio.

Biochimbank would then buy ZUNK bonds from the central bank's portfolio well below their minimum acceptable price with part of the money and possibly resell them later at a higher price to boost its capital.
The minimum acceptable price of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds issued in 1994 is now set at 45 percent of par.
The T-note issue is to be backed at a priority through proceeds from future sales of stakes in Bulbank and the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company, whichever comes first, the government decided.

Under a $509 million 14-month stand-by agreement approved by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) board late on Friday Bulgaria is to stabilise state banks prior to introduction of a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism, known as a currency board system, in June.

The system would require levs in circulation to be strictly matched to central bank foreign currency reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and preventing the printing of money.

Biochimbank is the only operating local state bank with a negative capital net worth and suffers a serious liquidity shortage that needs to be compensated from the budget and the central bank, bankers said.

The bank had a capital-to-risk assets ratio of five percent at the end of last year after it managed to collect some risk loans and received long-term government securities worth $81 million to boost its capital. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
